+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  DHARMIC FAMILY OVERVIEW                           |
|                                                                    |
|  HINDUISM              BUDDHISM             JAINISM    SIKHISM     |
|  ---------             --------             -------    -------     |
|  No founder;           Siddhartha           Mahavira   Guru Nanak  |
|  no single             Gautama              (~6th c    (1469-      |
|  authority.            (~5th c BCE)         BCE)       1539 CE)    |
|  Vedic roots,          Rejects Vedic        Rejects    Monotheist; |
|  vast diversity.       authority,           Vedas;     rejects     |
|  ~1.2 billion.         Atman concept.       ahimsa     caste.      |
|                       ~500 million.        central.   ~30 million. |
|                                             ~5 million.            |
|                                                                    |
|  SHARED CONCEPTS (with different meanings in each tradition):      |
|  karma, samsara, dharma, liberation (moksha/nirvana/mukti)         |
|                                                                    |
|  KEY DISPUTE: Does a permanent self (Atman) exist?                 |
|  Hinduism (mostly): YES — Atman = Brahman                          |
|  Buddhism: NO — anatta (no-self) is a core teaching                |
|  Jainism: YES — jiva (soul), but material, accumulates karma       |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------+

+---------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                   HINDU TEXTUAL LAYERS                              |
|                                                                     |
|  SHRUTI ("heard" — direct divine revelation)                        |
|  +-----------+------------------------------------------+           |
|  | VEDAS     | Four collections (~1500-900 BCE):        |           |
|  | (oldest)  | Rig Veda (hymns), Sama Veda (chants),   |           |
|  |           | Yajur Veda (ritual formulas),            |           |
|  |           | Atharva Veda (spells, healing)           |           |
|  +-----------+------------------------------------------+           |
|  | BRAHMANAS | Prose ritual commentaries on the Vedas   |           |
|  +-----------+------------------------------------------+           |
|  | ARANYAKAS | Forest treatises — transitional          |           |
|  +-----------+------------------------------------------+           |
|  | UPANISHADS| 108 philosophical texts (~800-200 BCE)   |           |
|  |           | The "Vedanta" (end/culmination of Vedas) |           |
|  |           | Brahman-Atman identity: tat tvam asi     |           |
|  |           | ("that thou art") — self = ultimate      |           |
|  +-----------+------------------------------------------+           |
|                                                                     |
|  SMRITI ("remembered" — secondary authority)                        |
|  Mahabharata (~400 BCE - 400 CE) — contains Bhagavad Gita          |
|  Ramayana (~500-300 BCE)                                            |
|  Puranas (18 major — narratives of gods, cosmology, genealogy)      |
|  Manu Smriti (law code — controversial for caste rules)             |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------+

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               FOUR NOBLE TRUTHS (Ariya Sacca)                    |
|                                                                  |
|  1. DUKKHA (suffering/unsatisfactoriness):                       |
|     All conditioned existence involves dukkha.                   |
|     Not just pain — the fundamental unsatisfactoriness           |
|     of impermanent, dependent phenomena.                         |
|                                                                  |
|  2. SAMUDAYA (arising/origin):                                   |
|     Dukkha arises from tanha (craving/thirst) —                  |
|     craving for sensual pleasure, existence, non-existence.      |
|     The Second Noble Truth is a causal claim.                    |
|                                                                  |
|  3. NIRODHA (cessation):                                         |
|     Dukkha can cease. Nirvana is the cessation of craving.       |
|     Not annihilation — cessation of the fires of greed,          |
|     hatred, delusion.                                            |
|                                                                  |
|  4. MAGGA (path):                                                |
|     The Noble Eightfold Path leads to that cessation.            |
|     Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right             |
|     Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right                |
|     Mindfulness, Right Concentration.                            |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|              BUDDHIST VEHICLES (YANA)                             |
|                                                                   |
|  THERAVADA ("way of the elders")                                  |
|  Pali Canon (Tipitaka). Southeast Asia (Sri Lanka, Thailand,      |
|  Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos). Individual liberation as nirvana.      |
|  Arhant ideal: achieve liberation for oneself.                    |
|                                                                   |
|       | Mahayana revolution (c.1st c BCE - 1st c CE)              |
|       v                                                           |
|  MAHAYANA ("great vehicle")                                       |
|  Bodhisattva ideal: delay final liberation to save all beings.    |
|  Sunyata (emptiness): all phenomena are empty of inherent         |
|  existence (Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka). Buddha-nature (tathata-      |
|  garba): all beings have Buddha-nature, capacity for awakening.   |
|  Vast literature: Prajnaparamita sutras, Lotus Sutra, etc.        |
|  East Asia: China, Korea, Japan.                                  |
|                                                                   |
|       | Vajrayana develops from Mahayana (~7th c CE onward)       |
|       v                                                           |
|  VAJRAYANA ("diamond vehicle")                                    |
|  Tantric practices: use of desire/aversion (not suppression)      |
|  as fuel for awakening. Mantra, mudra, mandala, visualization.    |
|  Lama (guru) lineage essential. Tibet, Mongolia, Bhutan.          |
|  Dalai Lama institution: Avalokiteshvara incarnation.             |
|  Tulku system: reincarnate teachers identified in childhood.      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
